prompts: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a polished landscape 1536x1024 educational illustration for a dark graphene science website. Dark warm charcoal background, copper honeycomb carbon sheets, restrained teal arrows, cream readable labels. Three left-to-right stages, ample spacing, realistic dimensional scientific illustration, not a chart. Carbon sheets must be hexagonal honeycomb networks, never square grids. Short labels only, no other text. Conceptual, not operating instructions. Show mechanical exfoliation. Left: thick graphite stack made of many honeycomb sheets. Middle: translucent adhesive tape curls upward lifting a thin top sheet from that stack, a clear peeling front. Right: a small thin honeycomb flake resting on a flat substrate. Exact stage labels: "Graphite", "Peel with tape", "Thin flake". No liquid.

Use case: scientific-educational. Create a polished landscape 1536x1024 educational illustration for a dark graphene science website. Three left-to-right stages, ample spacing, realistic dimensional scientific illustration, not a chart. Carbon sheets must be hexagonal honeycomb networks, never square grids. Short labels only, no other text. Conceptual, not operating instructions. Show liquid-phase exfoliation. Left: layered graphite particles entering a transparent beaker containing liquid. Middle: immersed mixing rotor and curved flow arrows shear layered particles apart; magnified inset clearly shows sideways sliding of honeycomb layers in liquid. Right: beaker containing dispersed thin honeycomb flakes of varying sizes and layer counts. Exact labels: "Graphite + liquid", "Shear mixing", "Dispersed flakes". Do not imply every particle is monolayer.

Use case: scientific-educational. Create a polished landscape 1536x1024 educational illustration for a dark graphene science website. Dark warm charcoal background, copper honeycomb carbon sheets, restrained teal arrows, cream readable labels. Three left-to-right stages, ample spacing, realistic dimensional scientific illustration, not a chart. Carbon sheets must be hexagonal honeycomb networks, never square grids. Short labels only, no other text. Conceptual, not operating instructions. Show oxidation-assisted exfoliation then reduction. Left: stacked graphite honeycomb layers. Middle: separated honeycomb sheets with teal oxygen-containing group markers attached, with a small label "Oxidise + exfoliate" above connecting arrow. Right: sheet with fewer teal markers and a few irregular holes, conveying reduced graphene oxide retains defects. Exact main labels: "Graphite", "Graphene oxide", "Reduced graphene oxide". Small arrow label between middle and right: "Reduce". Preserve copper carbon network; teal markers represent oxygen groups, not extra carbon.

Use case: scientific-educational. Create a polished landscape 1536x1024 educational illustration for a dark graphene science website. Dark warm charcoal background, copper honeycomb carbon sheets, restrained teal arrows, cream readable labels. Three left-to-right stages, ample spacing, realistic dimensional scientific illustration, not a chart. Carbon sheets must be hexagonal honeycomb networks, never square grids. Short labels only, no other text. Conceptual, not operating instructions. Show compressible-flow exfoliation (CFE). Left: carrier gas teal streamlines with small stacked graphite particles entering a wide inlet. Middle: cutaway converging-diverging nozzle with narrow throat and widening outlet; streamlines travel left to right, stacked particles carried through. Above nozzle show a large circular magnified conceptual inset of gas pushing copper honeycomb layers sideways with one separating, thin teal arrows along sheet surfaces. Right: collection chamber containing processed flakes with varying layer counts. Exact labels: "Gas + graphite", "Flow through nozzle", "Collect flakes". Inset label: "Sliding + separation". No liquid, no fire, no guaranteed single-layer output.

edits.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: educational website illustration. Edit the supplied illustration, preserving its 1536x1024 landscape layout, dark warm charcoal background, copper hexagonal honeycomb sheets, teal accents, three glass beakers, cream typography, left and right stages. Replace ONLY the middle shear-mixing mechanism with TIP SONICATION: a straight cylindrical metallic ultrasonic probe comes vertically from above and ends as a simple flat blunt tip immersed below the liquid surface. Absolutely no blades, propeller, impeller or rotor. Show localized fine cavitation bubbles and small teal acoustic wave arcs near the immersed probe tip, with irregular graphite sheets separating nearby; no broad rotational vortex arrows. Adjust the magnified inset to depict bubbles near separating copper honeycomb layers in liquid. Exact bottom labels: "Graphite + liquid", "Tip sonication", "Dispersed flakes". Retain varying flake sizes and layer counts, not all monolayers. Keep all text legible and apparatus fully in frame.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: educational website illustration. Edit only the downstream collection stage on the RIGHT of the supplied CFE schematic. Preserve exactly the left gas and graphite inlet, central converging-diverging nozzle, upper circular sliding-and-separation inset, dark background, copper sheets, teal streamlines, cream typography and 1536x1024 composition. Replace the tall swirling cyclone-like chamber with a compact horizontal downstream dry filter housing directly connected to the nozzle outlet. Show a clear cutaway: flake-bearing gas enters from left, irregular thin dark copper-edged flakes of varied sizes/layer counts accumulate on the upstream LEFT face of a vertical fine porous filter membrane; clean teal gas streamlines pass through the filter and continue to a short open outlet on the RIGHT. The membrane spans the housing, no flakes beyond it. A small modest powder deposit on the upstream side conveys collection, not a chamber of giant floating perfect hexagon sheets. Keep collector fully inside frame. No liquid, no swirling chamber, no bottom funnel, no disconnected vessel. Bottom labels remain exactly "Gas + graphite", "Flow through nozzle", "Collect flakes"; inset label "Sliding + separation". This is a conceptual filtration collector, not a specific experimental apparatus.
